correctness.rationale: For a p-strand braided pattern the winding number is p. The recent affine satellite formula gives a tau difference of binomial(p,2) times the framing difference throughout the stated high-framing range. Tau changes by at most one under a single crossing change, giving the same quantity as a lower bound for Gordian distance. A unit framing change inserts one full twist. The pure full twist factors into one conjugate of a braid-generator square for every unordered pair of strands; one crossing change kills each factor. Hence binomial(p,2) crossing changes realize a unit framing change and the two bounds agree. The quantifiers, threshold, orientation convention, and p at least two boundary are stated explicitly.

The close 2026 follow-up studies unknotting number rather than exact pairwise distance between framing values. The accepted statement additionally needs the independent full-twist crossing-change construction to prove sharpness, so it is not already implied as a stated Gordian theorem by either source. value.rationale: The result turns a newly available affine knot-Floer formula into an exact metric statement on an infinite family, rather than merely another invariant value. It proves that the obvious full-twist path is globally shortest and identifies a scaled isometric integer ray in the Gordian graph for every braided L-space satellite operator in the stated regime. This is structurally useful for comparing satellite families and is substantially stronger than a one-sided lower bound or a single unknotting-number estimate.
